normal_flow_topology_draft.summary: The topology represents a complex hospital discharge workflow. It includes routine discharge preparation, medication-related activities, home-care coordination, facility transfers, transport alternatives, discharge postponement, return to active treatment and discharge against medical advice.

nodes.name: Confirm preliminary clinical readiness
nodes.description: The responsible physician performs an initial assessment and determines whether the patient may enter the discharge preparation process.

nodes.name: Determine discharge disposition
nodes.description: The clinical team determines whether the planned discharge can continue, whether the patient must return to active treatment, or whether the patient intends to leave against medical advice.

nodes.name: Assess discharge complexity
nodes.description: The team identifies the clinical documentation, medication and continuity-of-care workstreams required for the discharge.

nodes.name: Prepare routine clinical documentation
nodes.description: The clinical team prepares the standard discharge letter, follow-up instructions, clinical reports and required certificates.

nodes.name: Perform medication reconciliation
nodes.description: Current medicines are compared with the intended post-discharge therapy to identify additions, discontinuations, substitutions and potential interactions.

nodes.name: Assess social and continuity-of-care needs
nodes.description: The team evaluates whether the patient can return home, requires organized home support, needs placement in another facility or currently has no safe discharge destination.

nodes.name: Finalize internal medication plan
nodes.description: The physician and hospital pharmacist finalize the post-discharge medication plan using resources available within
